title: Cokernel tail coordinates after prescribed invertible matrix operations
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and D:R^m→R^n a rectangular matrix, with ρ≤m and ρ≤n. Suppose P∈GL_n(R), Q∈GL_m(R) satisfy PDQ=J, where J_ij=1 if i=j<ρ and is zero otherwise. The categorical cokernel of D is isomorphic to R^(n−ρ), and the composite of its projection and this isomorphism sends x to the final n−ρ coordinates of Px. The statement includes m=0, n=0, ρ=0, and ρ=n.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), finite-presentation calculation; Stacks, algebra.tex lemma-tensor-product-exact; sites-modules.tex section-constant and section-tensor-product.

proof.text: For the rank matrix, compute each coordinate of Jx: it is x_i for i<ρ and zero otherwise. Its image is exactly the kernel of tail extraction; construct a preimage from the first ρ coordinates, padded with zeros.
Tail extraction is surjective, by zero padding. Use ModuleCat.isColimitCokernelCofork to identify the cokernel with the tail power.
Use PD=JQ inverse to obtain a commuting square of isomorphisms and transport the cokernel. The cokernel map projection equation gives tail(Px).

mathlib_searches.query: A constant sheaf module realization followed by scalar extension preserves a matrix cokernel and its quotient projection, and an invertible change of rows identifies the cokernel with the remaining coordinates

No duplicate of these normalized helpers.

lean.statement: theorem rankNormalCokernel {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {m n ρ : ℕ} (D : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) R) (hρn : ρ ≤ n) (hρm : ρ ≤ m) (P : GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) R) (Q : GeneralLinearGroup (Fin m) R) (hnorm : (P : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) * D * (Q : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) R) = fun i j ↦ if i.val = j.val ∧ i.val < ρ then 1 else 0) : ∃ a : cokernel (ModuleCat.ofHom (Matrix.toLin' D)) ≅ ModuleCat.of R (Fin (n - ρ) → R), ∀ (x : Fin n → R) (j : Fin (n - ρ)), a.hom (cokernel.π (ModuleCat.ofHom (Matrix.toLin' D)) x) j = (P : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R).mulVec x (Fin.cast (Nat.add_sub_of_le hρn) (Fin.natAdd ρ j))
